title: Abetting mutiny, or attempting to seduce a soldier, sailor or airman from his duty
old_text: Penalized abetting mutiny in the Army, Navy or Air Force, or attempting to seduce any officer or soldier from duty, with life imprisonment or up to 10 years and fine.
new_text: Penalizes abetting mutiny by any officer, soldier, sailor or airman in the armed forces of India, or attempting to seduce such person from allegiance or duty.
punishment_old: Imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine (IPC Section 131).
punishment_new: Imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine (BNS Section 159).
explanation: Guards military discipline and national defence by penalizing civilian or external attempts to instigate mutiny or subvert troop loyalty. Renumbered from IPC Section 131.

title: Abetment of mutiny, if mutiny is committed in consequence thereof
old_text: Penalized abetment of mutiny where mutiny is committed in consequence with death or life imprisonment or up to 10 years and fine.
new_text: Whoever abets the commission of mutiny, if mutiny is committed in consequence of that abetment, shall be punished with death or imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to ten years, and fine.
punishment_old: Death, or imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine (IPC Section 132).
punishment_new: Death, or imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine (BNS Section 160).
explanation: Mandates capital punishment or life imprisonment where civilian or external instigation successfully causes an active military mutiny to erupt. Renumbered from IPC Section 132.

title: Abetment of assault by soldier, sailor or airman on his superior officer, when in execution of his office
old_text: Penalized abetting an assault by an armed forces member on a superior officer in execution of office with imprisonment up to 3 years and fine.
new_text: Whoever abets an assault by an officer, soldier, sailor or airman on his superior officer being in the execution of his office, shall be punished with imprisonment up to three years, and fine.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 3 years, and fine (IPC Section 133).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to three years, and fine (BNS Section 161).
explanation: Upholds hierarchical command authority by punishing anyone who incites armed personnel to assault superior officers on duty. Renumbered from IPC Section 133.

title: Abetment of such assault, if assault committed
old_text: Penalized abetting such assault on a superior officer where the assault is committed in consequence with imprisonment up to 7 years and fine.
new_text: Whoever abets an assault by an officer, soldier, sailor or airman on his superior officer in execution of office, if such assault is committed in consequence, shall be punished with imprisonment up to seven years, and fine.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 7 years, and fine (IPC Section 134).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to seven years, and fine (BNS Section 162).
explanation: Elevates the punishment ceiling to seven years when the abetted physical attack upon a superior commanding officer actually takes place. Renumbered from IPC Section 134.

title: Abetment of desertion of soldier, sailor or airman
old_text: Penalized abetting the desertion of any soldier, sailor or airman from the armed forces with imprisonment up to 2 years or fine or both.
new_text: Whoever abets the desertion of any officer, soldier, sailor or airman in the Army, Navy or Air Force of India, shall be punished with imprisonment up to two years, or with fine, or with both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both (IPC Section 135).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to two years, or with fine, or with both (BNS Section 163).
explanation: Criminalizes inducing military personnel to abandon their posts or desert service. Renumbered from IPC Section 135.

title: Harbouring deserter
old_text: Penalized harbouring or concealing an armed forces deserter knowing them to be a deserter with imprisonment up to 2 years or fine or both, with spousal exception.
new_text: Whoever, knowing or having reason to believe that an officer, soldier, sailor or airman has deserted, harbours or conceals such deserter, shall be punished with imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both, with an exception for spouses.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both (IPC Section 136).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to two years, or with fine, or with both (BNS Section 164).
explanation: Penalizes sheltering military deserters while maintaining the marital exemption shielding a husband or wife harbouring their spouse. Renumbered from IPC Section 136.

title: Deserter concealed on board merchant vessel through negligence of master
old_text: Penalized the master of a merchant vessel on board which a deserter is concealed through negligence with a penalty fine up to ₹500.
new_text: The master or person in charge of a merchant vessel, on board of which any deserter from the armed forces is concealed through negligence or want of care, shall be liable to a penalty which may extend to three thousand rupees.
punishment_new: Penalty fine which may extend to three thousand rupees (BNS Section 165).
explanation: Imposes strict maritime oversight upon commercial vessel masters, raising the maximum negligence penalty sixfold from ₹500 to ₹3,000. Renumbered from IPC Section 137.

title: Abetment of act of insubordination by soldier, sailor or airman
old_text: Penalized abetting an act of insubordination if insubordination is committed in consequence with imprisonment up to 6 months or fine or both.
new_text: Whoever abets what he knows to be an act of insubordination by an officer, soldier, sailor or airman, shall, if such insubordination be committed in consequence, be punished with imprisonment up to six months, or fine, or both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine, or both (IPC Section 138).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to six months, or with fine, or with both (BNS Section 166).
explanation: Penalizes outside incitement leading to military disobedience or defiance of standing operational orders. Renumbered from IPC Section 138.

title: Persons subject to certain Acts
old_text: Exempted persons subject to the Army Act, Navy Act, or Air Force Act from punishment under this chapter for offences subject to court-martial jurisdiction.
new_text: Clarifies that no person subject to the Army Act, 1950, the Navy Act, 1957, or the Air Force Act, 1950, is subject to punishment under this Sanhita for any offence in this Chapter governed by military law.
explanation: Preserves the boundary between civilian penal courts and specialized military justice systems, ensuring court-martial precedence for service personnel. Renumbered from IPC Section 139.

title: Wearing garb or carrying token used by soldier, sailor or airman
old_text: Penalized unauthorized wearing of armed forces uniform or token with intent to deceive with imprisonment up to 3 months or fine up to ₹500, or both.
new_text: Whoever, not being a member of the Army, Navy or Air Force of India, wears any garb or carries any token resembling armed forces attire with intent that it may be believed he is such a member, shall be punished with imprisonment up to three months, or fine up to two thousand rupees, or both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 3 months, or fine up to ₹500, or both (IPC Section 140).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to three months, or with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees, or with both (BNS Section 168).
explanation: Penalizes civilian impersonation of armed forces personnel through unauthorized uniforms, insignias, or tokens, quadrupling the maximum fine from ₹500 to ₹2,000. Renumbered from IPC Section 140.
